sheets.name: Dialogue
sheets.comment: contains all information about a Dialogue System conversation used in the game. additional triggering and non-identifying information is handled by mapped metas

fields.name: completion_arc
fields.comment: this allows specifying a custom completion arc, otherwise the last primary arc is assumed

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: priority is shared across all eligible dialogue unless the dialogue category itself implies priority (eg final idle is always lower than quest, and gossip cannot appear outside of the gossip menu)

fields.name: has_player_initiated_question
fields.comment: this should be true for gossips and dynamic questions

sheets.name: ActorInteractionRule
sheets.comment:
this meta allows rules to automatically configure the interaction menu based on conditions in the gamestate. this is to simplify scripting of the interaction menu for certain quest steps (eg when first meeting an npc, we don't want to allow gossip until the introduction dialogue is played)
- things like preventing the npc from appearing in dates AT ALL before the introduction dialogue plays can be handled with dialogue gates
- when the player walks close enough to interact with an NPC the rules are checked to see if the interaction menu should be limited
- all interaction types are available at all times by default unless a rule causes limitations
- if multiple eligible limitations exist, the union set is chosen
- rules about dialogue types supersede rules for the interaction menu (eg gossip is never allowed when an actor is on a date)

fields.name: areas_allowed
fields.comment: if specified, the rule is only relevant in the specific areas. if unspecified, the rule applies everywhere that it is not specifically denied

fields.name: governing_rule
fields.comment: if set, the parent rule will be checked to determine if this rule is still eligible for consideration. governing rules change meaning somewhat as they pertain only to governed rules and not the type of entity the other rules in the meta are typically about. if the governing rule is checked and found to be violated, the governed rule is consider violated even if the governed rule would otherwise be valid. (this design allows defining rich rulesets that can also be deactivated partway through a game)

sheets.name: DialogueAvailabilityRule
sheets.comment:
this allows dialogue to be made available or not. it is a separate meta because it is possible to define multiple rules for a given dialogue, though such a situation is hopefully rare
*****DONT FORGET TO MIRROR CHANGES TO SpawnRule META*****

sheets.name: Area
sheets.comment: this meta identifies unity scenes (eg CentralForest) for use in rules and triggering

sheets.name: DialogueArc
sheets.comment: this is used a bit differently than other metas. it is a shared set of arc suffixes eg p1, i4, n9. this is useful for mapping certain things for advanced filtering and triggering. game side, arcs use a generated db name and savekey for a faux db lookup

fields.name: name
fields.comment: This is the arc name suffix ie p1, i5, n11. These conventions are consistent across all dialogues so an entry in this table can be reused for any number of dialogues.

fields.name: dialogue_filter
fields.comment: either dialogue filter OR trigger filter must be set. (this is enforced by the data layer and not the db.) dialogue filter causes the state trigger to fire on dialogue completion. trigger filter causes the state trigger to fire on trigger activation.

fields.name: trigger_filter
fields.comment: either dialogue filter OR trigger filter must be set. (this is enforced by the data layer and not the db.) dialogue filter causes the state trigger to fire on dialogue completion. trigger filter causes the state trigger to fire on trigger activation.

fields.name: invalidate_dialogues
fields.comment: this can also be modeled using availability rules and antievents, but it's cleaner to do it here for the select few cases of missable content (mostly easter eggs or parallel quest steps, eg no need to ask others about string once you get the shoelaces from Mabel)

fields.name: start_quests
fields.comment: this is automatically inferred for its own quests, so it is mainly provided to trigger other quests

fields.name: complete_quests
fields.comment: this is automatically inferred for its own quests, so it is mainly provided to trigger other quests

fields.name: manage_items
fields.comment: use manage items in combination with item quantities parallel array. use a positive integer to add items, a negative integer to remove items, or zero to consume items

fields.name: item_quantities_parallel
fields.comment: quantity array length needs to match manage items list length. all integers should be nonzero to add or remove, zero to consume whatever quantity exists in the inventory

fields.name: name
fields.comment: this isn't used by the game code. it's only for mapping to other db fields
